identity.title: Forklift Pre-Shift Inspection Log – Toyota 8FGU25 Unit FL-2 (Propane), Portland Warehouse, September 2026
identity.site: Portland — 4410 NW Front Ave, Portland, Oregon 97210

page_refs.jurisdiction: page 1 (header cites OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7)); Oregon comes from the company's state

scan.summary: This is the company's own daily pre-shift inspection log for one propane forklift (unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse for September 2026. It is the record showing the truck was checked before use, as the forklift rule requires; Oregon OSHA adopts that rule and adds its own forklift rules in OAR 437-002-0227. A log is judged on whether it is complete and up to date. This one has missing days while the truck was running, a horn defect with no repair or out-of-service record, no entries after Sep 18, and a blank supervisor sign-off.
scan.freshness_note: The last entry is Sep 18, 2026, which is 9 days before today (Sep 27). The weekdays Sep 21–25 have no entries. Ask whether a continuation page or a later version of the log exists. If it does not, the truck was either not used or was used without inspection after Sep 18.

gaps.title: No inspections logged for Sep 3 and Sep 4 even though the truck ran
gaps.description: The log skips from Sep 2 to Sep 7. Sep 3 (Thu) and Sep 4 (Fri) are weekdays (inferred from the calendar). The hour meter goes up 15 hours from 4,819 on Sep 2 to 4,834 on Sep 7, about two days of use at this truck's usual 6–7 hours a day. So the truck ran on days with no inspection recorded.
gaps.fix: Ask the operators and supervisor whether inspections were done on paper somewhere else or not done at all. Do not back-fill entries. Write a short dated note explaining the gap, remind operators that the check is required before use, and have the supervisor check the log every day.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (examine before placing in service, at least daily), adopted in Oregon through OAR 437 Division 2, Subdivision N; OAR 437-002-0227 holds Oregon's additional forklift rules
gaps.locator: page 1, between the Sep 2 and Sep 7 rows
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Horn defect on Sep 9 with no out-of-service or repair record
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn is marked X with the note 'Horn not working'. Nothing records the truck being tagged out, who repaired it, or when. The hour meter goes from 4,847 on Sep 9 to 4,853 on Sep 10, so the truck appears to have run about 6 hours after the defect was found (inferred). The next day's horn tick is the only sign it was fixed.
gaps.fix: Find or create the repair record: work order or invoice, who fixed it, and the date and time. If the truck ran with a dead horn, write that down and correct it with the operator. Add a 'defect reported to / action taken / returned to service by' line to the log form.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (do not place in service if a condition adversely affects safety; report and correct defects) and 29 CFR 1910.178(p)(1) (a defective or unsafe truck is taken out of service until restored to safe condition). I checked both paragraph numbers against my knowledge of the standard and am confident in them, but I did not re-read the eCFR text this session.
gaps.locator: page 1, Sep 9 row, Horn column and Notes

gaps.title: No entries after Sep 18
gaps.description: The last entry is Sep 18. Today is Sep 27, and the weekdays Sep 21–25 have no entries. Either the log was not kept after Sep 18, the truck was out of use, or a later page was not included in this file.
gaps.fix: Ask for any later page. If the truck was out of service, write that down (for example, 'FL-2 out of service Sep 21–__, reason'). If it ran, the inspections are missing. Make sure daily logging continues.

gaps.title: Supervisor review line blank
gaps.description: The form has a supervisor review signature and date, and both are empty. The OSHA rule does not itself require a supervisor signature. But the form calls for one, and a review would likely have caught the missing days and the horn follow-up.
gaps.fix: Have the warehouse supervisor review and sign the log (weekly and at month end), writing down any follow-up on gaps and defects.

deadlines.source_line: Inspection per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): examine before each shift; do not use if a defect affects safety.
